n4784815dedc.s: Which of the following rebellions occurred earliest?
n4784815dedc.x: The Gulugonda revolt took place in 1845-48, before Phadke's revolt (1879), Khudiram Bose's episode (1908) and Alluri's Rampa rebellion (1922-24).

nd6aef4900f8.s: How many of the 19 village officers of the Pedanandipadu firka resigned during the 1922 no-tax campaign?
nd6aef4900f8.x: 18 of the 19 village officers in the firka resigned during the campaign.

n704f92f0b56.s: In which year was Sri Sri's Mahaprasthanam published?
n704f92f0b56.x: Mahaprasthanam was published in 1950; its first poem Jayabheri dates to 1933 and the Virasam phase began in 1970.

new.s: At whose invitation did Bipin Chandra Pal tour Andhra in 1907?
new.x: Pal toured Andhra in 1907 at the invitation of Mutnuri Krishna Rao, editor of the Krishna Patrika. Kopalle Hanumantha Rao was his host at Machilipatnam.

new.s: Who hosted Bipin Chandra Pal at Machilipatnam during his 1907 tour?
new.x: Kopalle Hanumantha Rao hosted Pal at Machilipatnam and founded the Andhra Jatheeya Vidya Parishad there on 17 Nov 1907.

new.s: Which AICC meeting of 5 Nov 1921 allowed provincial committees to start civil disobedience, including no-tax?
new.x: The Delhi AICC of 5 Nov 1921 let provincial committees start civil disobedience including no-tax, which Guntur took up.

new.s: From which university did Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya take his M.A. (Hons) in Economics in 1916?
new.x: Duggirala took an M.A. (Hons) in Economics from the University of Edinburgh in 1916 and was Secretary of the Edinburgh Indian Association.

new.s: After the Non-Cooperation Movement, Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya joined which party as an Andhra secretary?
new.x: After the NCM he joined the Swaraj Party of C.R. Das and Motilal Nehru as an Andhra secretary.

new.s: By how much did the yearly tax rise when Chirala and Perala were made a municipality?
new.x: Making Chirala-Perala a municipality (Jan 1920) raised the yearly tax from Rs 4,000 to Rs 40,000.

new.s: Who was the first woman jailed in the Chirala-Perala movement?
new.x: Ravuri Alivelu Mangatayaramma was the first woman jailed; Duvvuri Subbamma was also arrested but was not the first.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Chirala-Perala movement:
1. On 25 April 1921, 13,572 of 15,326 residents left the town.
2. The Ramnagar camp with its parallel self-rule lasted about 11 months.
3. Duggirala was tried by Rutherford at Srikakulam.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: All three are correct: the midnight exodus of 25 April 1921, the 11-month Ramnagar self-rule, and Duggirala's trial by Rutherford at Srikakulam.

new.s: The Palnadu movement of 1921-22 refused which tax?
new.x: Palnadu refused pullari, the grazing (grass) tax on forest land; Pedanandipadu refused land revenue.

new.s: Who led the Palnadu pullari (forest) satyagraha of 1921-22?
new.x: Kanneganti Hanumanthu led it and was killed in police firing at Minchalapadu; Unnava Lakshminarayana backed it.

new.s: Which tax did the Pedanandipadu no-tax campaign of 1922 refuse to pay?
new.x: Pedanandipadu refused land revenue, when the first instalment fell due in January-February 1922.

new.s: The volunteer force of Parvataneni Veeraiah Chowdary in the Pedanandipadu campaign was called:
new.x: Shanti Sena belonged to Parvataneni (Pedanandipadu); Ramadandu was Duggirala's corps at Chirala-Perala.

new.s: Which Revenue Board member blamed the Congress and was sent to Guntur during the no-tax campaign?
new.x: Revenue Board member L.T. Harris blamed the Congress and was sent to Guntur; Rutherford's plan to ban the Shanti Sena was rejected.

new.s: Chirala, Perala and Pedanandipadu all lay in which taluka of Guntur district?
new.x: Chirala, Perala and Pedanandipadu were all in Bapatla taluka of Guntur district.

new.s: Rekapalle, scene of the 1879 revolt, lay in which taluk of Godavari district?
new.x: Rekapalle lay in Bhadrachalam taluk, Godavari district, which was taken from the Nizam and joined Madras Presidency in 1874.

new.s: Minchalapadu, where Kanneganti Hanumanthu was killed, lies in which area of Guntur district?
new.x: Minchalapadu is a Palnadu village of Guntur district, scene of the pullari movement.

new.s: 'Begar', a grievance of the Agency tribes, meant:
o: Forced unpaid coolie labour for road building
Voluntary paid labour for road building
new.x: Begar was forced unpaid coolie labour for road building, not voluntary paid labour.

new.s: Which local official's excesses were the spark of the Rampa Rebellion of 1922-24?
new.x: Tahsildar Bastian's excesses were the spark; Madhava Bhupati was the Munsubdar of the 1879-80 revolt.

new.s: Who burnt the Addateegala police station in the Rampa revolt of 1879-80?
new.x: Dwarabandala Chandrayya, a leader of the 1879-80 Rampa revolt, burnt the Addateegala police station.

new.s: Raja Vijayarama Raju of Vizianagaram was killed in 1794 at:
new.x: Raja Vijayarama Raju was killed at Padmanabham on 8 July 1794.

new.s: The Gulugonda tribal revolt (1845-48) was led by:
new.x: The Gulugonda revolt of Vizag (1845-48) was led by Chinna Bhupathi.

new.s: Which associate of Alluri Sitarama Raju later became an MP in 1952?
new.x: Gam Mallu Dora, Raju's 'right hand', was arrested in 1923, given a life term and became an MP in 1952; Gantam Dora was killed in 1924.

new.s: Alluri Sitarama Raju was shot at Koyyuru in 1924 in the presence of:
new.x: Raju was captured by Jamadar Kanchu Meenan and shot at Koyyuru before Major Goodall on 7 May 1924.

new.s: Which British officers were killed at Damanapalli ghat on 24 Sept 1922?
new.x: Scott Coward and Heiter were killed at Damanapalli ghat on 24 Sept 1922.

new.s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Panjerighat – Direct battle with British forces
Peddagaddapalem – First defeat of Raju's forces
new.x: Koyyuru is where Raju was shot; his tomb (samadhi) is at Krishnadevipeta.

new.s: The officer who arrested Gam Mallu Dora was:
new.x: Keirns arrested Gam Mallu Dora in 1923.

new.s: Who was known as 'Desabhakta'?
new.x: Konda Venkatappayya was called Desabhakta; Desoddharaka was Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao.

new.s: The title 'Desoddharaka', given by the Andhra Mahasabha, belonged to:
new.x: Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao received the title Desoddharaka from the Andhra Mahasabha.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched?
new.x: Andhra Shivaji is usually Parvataneni Veeraiah Chowdary; Duggirala's title is Andhra Ratna.

new.s: Who was the first Telugu woman to give all her ornaments to the Tilak Swaraj Fund?
new.x: Maganti Annapurnamma gave all her ornaments to the Tilak Swaraj Fund and burnt foreign goods.

new.s: Who founded the Andhra Mahila Sabha at Madras in 1938?
new.x: Durgabai, who translated Gandhi's speech at Kakinada in April 1921, founded the Andhra Mahila Sabha (Madras, 1938).

new.s: Yamini Purna Tilakam is associated with:
new.x: Yamini Purna Tilakam is linked with the Guntur hartals.

new.s: The ban on the Hyderabad State Congress, imposed by the Nizam in 1938, was lifted in:
new.x: The Nizam banned the Hyderabad State Congress in 1938; the ban was lifted in 1946.

new.s: Students rusticated in the Osmania University Vandemataram movement of 1938 were admitted by:
new.x: About 350 students, among them P.V. Narasimha Rao, were rusticated and admitted by Nagpur University.

new.s: The daily 'Swarajya' (1921) was started by:
new.x: Tanguturi Prakasam started the Swarajya daily on 29 Oct 1921; Chilakamarti edited Desamata.

new.s: Who founded the Andhra Patrika?
new.x: Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao founded the Andhra Patrika; Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao was its first editor.

new.s: Sharada Niketan at Guntur, for girls' education, was founded by:
new.x: Unnava Lakshminarayana founded Sharada Niketan, Guntur, with his wife Lakshmibayamma.

new.s: The song 'Kallumanandoy' was written by:
new.x: 'Kallumanandoy' is by Gollapudi Sitarama Sastri; 'Veera gandham' is Tripuraneni Ramaswamy's.

new.s: Who is regarded as the first Telugu national poet?
new.x: Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham, editor of Desamata, is the first Telugu national poet.

new.s: According to C. Narayana Reddy, the first nationalist song in Telugu was:
new.x: C. Narayana Reddy named 'Melukonumi Bharata Putruda' (Andhra Bharati, Oct 1909) as the first nationalist song.

new.s: In 'Bharata khandambu chakkani paadi aavu', India is pictured as:
o: A cow whose milk the British were taking
new.x: Chilakamarti pictured India as a cow whose milk the British were taking; his later verse called India one big prison.

new.s: The song 'Veera gandham tecchinaramu' was written by:
new.x: 'Veera gandham tecchinaramu' (Salt Satyagraha era) is Tripuraneni Ramaswamy's; 'Maakoddee Tella Doratanamu' is Garimella's.

new.s: 'Kollayi gattithenemi maa Gandhi' was written by:
new.x: Basavaraju Apparao, a Bhavakavitvam poet, wrote the Gandhi song 'Kollayi gattithenemi'.

new.s: Gurajada Apparao's play Kanyasulkam was first staged in 1892 at:
new.x: Kanyasulkam was first staged in 1892 at Vizianagaram.

new.s: Gurajada's Mutyala Saralu is noted for pioneering:
o: A colloquial metre in Telugu verse
Free verse of the Abhyudaya type
new.x: Mutyala Saralu pioneered a colloquial metre (mutyala saram) in Telugu verse.

new.s: Rayaprolu Subbarao drew his Bhava Kavitvam from which poets?
new.x: Rayaprolu founded Bhava Kavitvam drawing on Shelley and Keats.

new.s: Progressive writers such as Sri Sri criticised the romanticism of Bhava Kavitvam as:
new.x: Abhyudaya writers such as Sri Sri called Bhava Kavitvam's romanticism 'escapist'.

new.s: Garimella Satyanarayana was born at Gonedapadu in which present district?
new.x: Garimella was born at Gonedapadu, Narasannapeta taluk, Srikakulam.

new.s: Garimella's song 'Maakoddee Tella Doratanamu' grew to how many lines?
new.x: The song grew to 162 lines, was copied a thousand times and was praised by Gandhi.

new.s: Adipudi Somanatha Rao's Japan Charitra was dedicated to:
new.x: Japan Charitra was dedicated to the Raja of Munagala, who named his sons Togo and Nogi.

new.s: How many students were arrested in Vizag for staging Panchala Parabhavam?
new.x: 25 students in Vizag were arrested for staging Damaraju Pundarikakshudu's Panchala Parabhavam.

new.s: Krovvidi Lingaraju was jailed for sedition under Sec. 124A in 1931 for:
new.x: Krovvidi Lingaraju's Veerabali (1931) led to his jailing under Sec. 124A.

new.s: Malapalli (1922) by Unnava Lakshminarayana was:
new.x: Malapalli (1922) was banned by the Madras government.

new.s: Who was called 'Telugu Lenka'?
new.x: Tummala Sitaramamurthy was called Telugu Lenka (G2 2012).

new.s: The title 'Kavi Kokila' is chiefly associated with:
new.x: Kavi Kokila is Duvvuri Ramireddy (Jashuva also got it in 1936); Devulapalli Krishna Sastri is Andhra Shelley.

new.s: Gurram Jashuva received the title 'Navayuga Kavi Chakravarti' in:
new.x: Jashuva got Kavi Kokila (1936), Navayuga Kavi Chakravarti (1946), Madhura Kavi Srinatha (1952) and Viswakavi Samrat (1964).

new.s: Which work of Viswanatha Satyanarayana won the Sahitya Akademi award?
new.x: Veyipadagalu won the Sahitya Akademi; Ramayana Kalpavrikshamu won the Jnanpith.

new.s: The first psychological novel in Telugu is:
new.x: T. Gopichand's Asamarthuni Jeevitha Yatra (1947) is the first psychological novel; Rajasekhara Charitram is the first Telugu novel.

new.s: Which work is the key text of Sri Sri's revolutionary (post-1970) Viplava phase?
new.x: Maro Prasthanam marks Sri Sri's revolutionary post-1970 phase; Mahaprasthanam is the Abhyudaya text.

new.s: The event that sparked the formation of Virasam was:
o: Sri Sri's Shashtipurti at Vizag, Feb 1970
new.x: Sri Sri's Shashtipurti (60th birthday) at Vizag in Feb 1970 was the spark for Virasam.

new.s: The first conference of Arasam (1943) was held at:
new.x: Arasam's first conference was held at Tenali, presided over by Tapi Dharma Rao.

new.s: Who presided over the first conference of Arasam?
new.x: Tapi Dharma Rao presided over Arasam's first conference at Tenali; Premchand presided over the AIPWA founding at Lucknow.

new.s: Arasam was the Telugu counterpart of which body?
new.x: Arasam was the Telugu counterpart of the AIPWA (1936, Lucknow).

new.s: Sri Sri co-founded the Sahiti Samiti at Vizag with:
new.x: Sri Sri's early body Sahiti Samiti was co-founded with Puripanda Appalaswamy.

new.s: Sri Sri was the founding President of which organisation?
new.x: Sri Sri was the founding President of Virasam (July 1970, Hyderabad).

new.s: Sri Sri's autobiography is titled:
new.x: Anantham is Sri Sri's autobiography; Siprali has the Sirisirimuvva satakam and limericks.

new.s: Who wrote the preface to Mahaprasthanam?
new.x: Chalam wrote the preface; the book was dedicated to Kompella Janardhana Rao.

new.s: Arudra's Tvamevaham (1948-49) deals with:
new.x: Arudra, Sri Sri's nephew, wrote Tvamevaham on the Telangana struggle.

new.s: Who was the Vice-President of Virasam in 1970?
new.x: Kodavatiganti Kutumba Rao was Vice-President of Virasam in 1970.

new.s: Firdausi, a laghu kavyam, was written by:
new.x: Gabbilam and Firdausi are Gurram Jashuva's, not Sri Sri's.

new.s: Who is known as 'Yuga Kavi'?
new.x: Yuga Kavi is Gunturu Seshendra Sarma; Sri Sri is Mahakavi.

new.s: The title 'Kavi Samrat' belongs to:
new.x: Viswanatha Satyanarayana is Kavi Samrat; Sri Sri is Mahakavi.

new.s: Besides Sri Sri, which poet was also called 'Mahakavi'?
new.x: Boyi Bhimanna was also called Mahakavi.

new.s: In which year did Krovvidi Lingaraju translate Gorky's The Mother as Amma?
new.x: Krovvidi Lingaraju's Amma, the Telugu translation of Gorky's The Mother, came out in 1934.

new.s: The Viswa Sahityamala, a publisher of world and leftist literature, was run by:
new.x: Viswa Sahityamala was run by the Mahidhara brothers; Gadde Lingayya ran the Adarsha Grantha Mandali.

new.s: Praja Natya Mandali (1943) was the Andhra wing of:
new.x: Praja Natya Mandali was the Andhra wing of the Indian People's Theatre Association.

new.s: Jana Natya Mandali (1971) grew out of the Art Lovers group of:
new.x: Jana Natya Mandali grew from Gaddar and B. Narsinga Rao's Art Lovers (1970).
